pairs.question: Punicas enim naues ex Sicilia accitas id posse facere: suas, quae sinu exiguo intus inclusae essent, cum claustra portus hostis haberet, quem ad modum inde in apertum mare euasuras?
pairs.derivation: The Tarentines object that, while summoned Punic ships could break the blockade, their own ships are shut in a narrow inlet with the enemy holding the harbor mouth, and ask how (quem ad modum) these could get out to open sea. The question span keeps the contrasting clause about the Punicae naues so that 'suas' has a referent. Hannibal answers directly: stripped the framing 'inquit Hannibal'; the answer is his first sentence 'Euadent' (= they will get out), stopping at the first full stop before he turns to elaborating his method (dragging the ships on wagons through the city: 'multa, quae impedita natura sunt, consilio expediuntur...').
